                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>NOw the men of Israel had sworn <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">In the beginning of this War, after the whole Tribe had espoused the quarrel of the Men of Gibeah, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 20. 13, 14</ns0:note> in Mizpeh, saying, There shall not any of us give his daughter unto Benjamin to wise <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">They do not (as some suppose) here swear the utter extirpation of the Tribe, which fell out beyond their ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pectation, <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 21. 3, 6. but only not to give their Daugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters to those Men who should survive; justly esteeming them for their harbarous Villany, to be as bad as the worst of Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thens with whom they were forbidden to Marry. In this Case the <ns0:hi>Benjamites</ns0:hi> might have Married among themselves, if any of their Men and Women were left alive.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And the people came to the house of God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Partly to mourn for the common loss; and partly, to ask counsel from God about the repairing of it.</ns0:note>, and abode there till even before God, and lift up their voices and wept sore.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And said, O LORD God of Israel, Why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Why hast thou given them up to such wickedness, and us to such rage, that the whole Tribe should be in a manner lost! Hence it appears, that they did not swear to root them all out, as is further manifest from the different matter and words of this Oath, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 1. which only denied them their Daughters in Marriage; and that concerning the people of other Tribes who joyned not with them in this business, which was, that they should <ns0:hi>be put to death, v.</ns0:hi> 5. And their sparing of those 600 Men in the Rock <ns0:hi>Rimmon,</ns0:hi> v. 13, 14. plainly shews, that they were not obliged by any Oath or Vow to extirpate them.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people rose early, and built there an altar <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Not for a Monument of the Victory, as some say, but for Sacrifices, as the next words shew. <ns0:hi>Qu.</ns0:hi> What need was there of this, when the ordinary Altar was there, to which also they seem to be restrained, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 16. 2? <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> They are not there restrained to one Altar, but to one place of Worship, as is expressed; and therefore there might be in that place more Altars than one, when the Multitude of Sacrifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces so required, which was the case, 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 8. 64. and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably at this time, when all the Tribes being met, they had many Sacrifices to offer, some in common for all, and some peculiar to every Tribe. Nay, other Altars might be, and oft-times were Erected in other places, by Divine Direction or Dispensation; as <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 6. 24, 26. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 7. 9, 17. and 11. 15. and 16. 2, 5.</ns0:note>, and offered burnt-offerings, and peace<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>offerings.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And the children of Israel said, Who <ns0:hi>is there</ns0:hi> among all the tribes of Israel, that came not up with the congregation unto the LORD? for they had made a great oath <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> A solemn Oath joyned with some terrible Execrati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on against the Offenders herein.</ns0:note> concerning him that came not up to the LORD to Mizpeh, saying, He shall surely be put to death <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Because by refusing to execute the Vengeance due to such Malefactors, they were justly presumed guilty of their Crime, and therefore liable to the same Punishment, as was the case of that City that would not deliver up an Idolater dwelling among them, to Justice.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And the children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Not for the War which was just, and necessary, and good; but for their immoderate severity in the Execution of it, and for the dreadful consequences of it.</ns0:note>, and said, There is one tribe cut off from Israel this day:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 How shall we do for wives for them that re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />main, seeing we have sworn by the LORD that we will not give them of our daughters to wives?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And they said, What one <ns0:hi>is there</ns0:hi> of the tribes of Israel, that came not up to Mizpeh to the LORD? And behold, there came none to the camp from Jabesh-gilead <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">A City in <ns0:hi>Gilead,</ns0:hi> and in the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Manasseh;</ns0:hi> of which see 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 11. 1, 3, 9, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and 31. 11, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> to the assembly.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 For the people were numbred, and behold, <ns0:hi>there were</ns0:hi> none of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead there.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And the congregation sent thither twelve thousand men of the valiantest, and commanded them, saying, Go, and smite the inhabitants of Ja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />besh-gilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the children <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Who in such publick and scandalous Crimes were for the greater Terrour of such Transgressors, and prevention of the like Sins, oft involved in the same Punishment with the men, as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 13. 15. <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 7. 24, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And this <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the thing that ye shall do, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Numb. 31<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> Ye shall utterly destroy every male, and every wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man that <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the lying with man.</ns0:note> hath lien by man <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">But not the Virgins, as appears from the next Verses. It is questionable, whether they were not obliged to destroy these also by vertue of their Oath, and of Gods express Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand concerning Devoted Persons, such as these certainly were, that they should <ns0:hi>surely be put to death,</ns0:hi> Levit. 27. 29. which was also particularly enjoyned and practised in such Cases, as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> But the natural and necessary duty of preserving a Tribe from total Ruine, might seem to render the case difficult and doubtful, and incline their Opi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nions, as well as their Affections, to the more favourable side. And it may be, the Lord, whom they were here consulting with upon all their occasions, gave them a Dispensation thus to do, though that be not expressed; which is the case of many other things which were done, though not Recorded; as this very Oath was omitted in its proper place, and had not been Recorded if this extraordinary occasion had not been offered.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:211" />12 And they found among the inhabitants of Ja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />besh-gilead, four hundred <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> young women Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gins.</ns0:note> young virgins <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Not Married, yet marriageable: it is probable, there were other and younger Virgins; but whether they were slain or spared, Scripture determines not, and the Learned do not agree. But these could not serve the present and urgent oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion, and therefore he takes notice onely of these 400 which were of riper Age.</ns0:note> that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And the whole congregation sent <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>pake and cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led.</ns0:note> to speak to the children of Benjamin that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> in the rock Rimmon, and to call <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> proclaim peace.</ns0:note> peaceably unto them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And Benjamin <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The poor remainders of the Tribe of Benjamin.</ns0:note> came again at that time, and they gave them wives which they had saved alive of the women of Jabesh-gilead: and yet so they sufficed them not.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And the people repented them for Benja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />min <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Were yet more grieved upon this unhappy disappoint<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, for they supposed here would have been Wives suffici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ent for them.</ns0:note>, because that the LORD had made a breach <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Benjamites</ns0:hi> were the onely Authors of the Sin, but God was the chief Author of the Punish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, and the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were but his Executioners.</ns0:note> in the tribes of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ Then the elders of the congregation said, How shall we do for Wives for them that remain <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">For the 200 who are yet unprovided of Wives.</ns0:note>? seeing the women are destroyed out of Benjamin:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And they said, <ns0:hi>There must be</ns0:hi> an inheritance for them that be escaped out of Benjamin <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The Inheritance promised by <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and given by <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> to the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Benjamin,</ns0:hi> doth all of it belong to those few which remain of that Tribe, and cannot be Possessed by any other Tribe; and therefore we are obliged to procure Wives for them all, that they may make up this breach, and be capable of Possessing and managing all their Land: that this Tribe, and their Inheritance may not be con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />founded with, or swallowed up by any of the rest. Heb. <ns0:hi>the inheritance</ns0:hi> (to wit, belonging to the whole Tribe of <ns0:hi>Benjamin</ns0:hi>) is, or belongs to <ns0:hi>them that be escaped of Benja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />min.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 Howbeit we may not give them wives of our daughters; for the children of Israel have sworn, saying, Cursed <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> he that giveth a wife to Benjamin <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> To this Generation of <ns0:hi>Benjamites</ns0:hi> who have made themselves guilty of this foul Wickedness: but this Oath did not extend to their Posterity. And some think it had another exception, to wit, unless the surviving <ns0:hi>Benjamites</ns0:hi> could not otherwise be supplied with wives.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 Then they said, Behold, <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> a feast of the LORD in Shiloh <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from year to year.</ns0:note> yearly <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">On the three solemn Feasts, in which they used some honest and holy Recreations; among which; Dancing was one, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 15. 20. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 18. 6. and 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 6. 14. and probably it was the Feast of Tabernacles, which they did Celebrate with more than ordinary joy, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 16. 13, 14, 15.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>in a place</ns0:hi> which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> on the north-side of Beth-el <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>Which is on the north of Bethel. Which</ns0:hi> doth not relate to <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> which was so known a place, that it was frivolous to describe it by such circumstances, even by pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces much less known than it self; but to the <ns0:hi>Feast,</ns0:hi> which as to that part or exercise of the Feast here especially con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerned and mentioned, to wit, the Dancing of the Virgins, was not celebrated in <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> but in a Neighbouring place more convenient for that purpose.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> towards the sun-rising.</ns0:note> on the east-side <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> on<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> of the high-way that goeth from Beth-el to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Therefore they commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, Go, and lie in wait in the vine<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yards:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And see, and behold, if the daughters of Shiloh <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">By whom he may possibly understand not those onely who were born or settled Inhabitants there, (as many con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceive) but all those who were come thither upon this occa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion, and for a time sojourned there: For although only the Males were obliged to go up the Three solemn Feasts; yet it is apparent, that the Women had liberty to go, and those who were most devout did usually go, and others upon spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial reasons or occasions: See 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 1. 7, 21, 22, 24. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2. 22, 23, 41, 42, 43. And it may be justly presumed, especi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally concerning those women that lived at no great distance from the place of Publick Worship, that they came thither in great numbers. Moreover, the <ns0:hi>daughters of Shiloh,</ns0:hi> strict<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly so called, are not onely they that liyed in that Town or City, bu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n the Country belonging to it, which oft comes under the name of the City to which it belongs. And these may be here particularly named, because though others might come, yet they were under great obligations to come, because of their nearness to the place.</ns0:note> come out to dance in dances, then come ye out of the vineyards <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Which were near to their Dancing-place.</ns0:note>, and catch ye every man his wife of the daughters of Shiloh <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Take them away by force or violence. Which they might the better do, because mixed Dances were not used by the People of God in their Solem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nities, but the Women danced by themselves, and therefore were more liable to this Rape.</ns0:note>, and go to the land of Benjamin.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And it shall be when their fathers, or their brethren come unto us to complain, that we will say unto them, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> Gratisie us in them.</ns0:note> Be favourable unto them <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Pass by their offence, if not for their sakes, whom necessi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty forced to this course; yet for our sakes, and indeed for your own sakes; for both you and we have done them a great injury in Prosecuting them with so much fury, as to en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />danger the utter extinction of the whole Tribe: and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore this is the least we can do by way of reparation.</ns0:note> for our sakes: because we reserved not to each man his wife in the war <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, First, in the War with <ns0:hi>Iabesh-Gilead,</ns0:hi> wherein they should have taken care to reserve a sufficient number, which they might have done, by sparing either so many of the Mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried Women as were necessary, who, their former Husbands being slain, might have been married to those <ns0:hi>Benjamites;</ns0:hi> or as many of the younger Virgins, who within a little time might have been Married to them; whom many suppose that they flew. Or, Secondly, in the War with the <ns0:hi>Benjamites,</ns0:hi> in which they acknowledge their cruelty in destroying the wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men with such fury, as not to leave a competent number for the Men which were left. See <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 20. 48.</ns0:note>: for ye did not give unto them at this time, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> ye should be guilty <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Qu.</ns0:hi> Whether this did really discharge them from their Oath? 1. <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> It seems to excuse those Parents of these Virgins who were not acquainted with the Plot, and did neither directly nor indi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rectly give their Daughters to them, but they were taken away by force, without their knowledge and consent. If it be said, those Parents might and should have retaken their Daughters from them; it may be replied, that they could not do so before they were corrupted, and the Rulers of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> would not assist them with their Power to recover them. And it is a Maxime, That many things which ought not to be done, when once they are done, should not be undone. And for those Parents who were conscious of the Design, it is probable they kept their Daughters at home to avoid this. Secondly, Either the Oath was made with an Exception of the Case of the Total Extirpation of a Tribe, or it was a rash Oath to do what was out of their Power, or what they could not lawfully do; to wit, utterly to destroy a Tribe out of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> which therefore they here speak of with horror, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3, 6. and if so, as they Sinned in making it, so they were not obliged to keep it; it being an acknowledged truth, That Rash and Sinful Oaths are better broken than kept. Thirdly, Yet they cannot be wholly excused from Sin in this matter; for as it was folly to take such an Oath as it is ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressed, so the manner of freeing themselves from their own Snare, is fraudulent and injurious to the Parents, in disposing of their Children without their consent.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
